gloss: living in two environments (water and land)

definitions.gloss: amphibious; living both in water and on land
definitions.explanation: A compound element meaning "living in two environments," built from {両|りょう} (both) + {生|せい} (life, living). It almost never stands alone, appearing instead inside compounds such as {両生類|りょうせいるい} (amphibians).

examples.japanese: {両生|りょうせい}⟦{類|るい}→類：15121_rui⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{水中|すいちゅう}→水中：13310_suichuu⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{陸上|りくじょう}→陸上：09245_rikujou⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{生活|せいかつ}できる→生活する：01839_seikatsusuru⟧。
examples.english: Amphibians can live in both water and on land.

examples.japanese: {両生|りょうせい}⟦{類|るい}→類：15121_rui⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{幼生期|ようせいき}にえら⟦{呼吸|こきゅう}→呼吸：02754_kokyuu⟧をする。
examples.english: Amphibians breathe through gills during their larval stage.

examples.japanese: 「{両生|りょうせい}」という⟦{言葉|ことば}→言葉：02880_kotoba⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧「{両生|りょうせい}⟦{類|るい}→類：15121_rui⟧」⟦{以外|いがい}→以外：01297_igai⟧ではあまり⟦{使|つか}われない→使う：00473_tsukau⟧。
examples.english: The word "ryōsei" is rarely used outside the compound "amphibian" (ryōseirui).

notes:
{両生|りょうせい} literally means "living both ways," describing an organism that lives in water and on land. It is a bound compound element, not a free-standing word.

COMPOUNDS:
- {両生|りょうせい}⟦{類|るい}→類：15121_rui⟧: amphibians (frogs, toads, newts, salamanders)
- {両生|りょうせい}⟦{的|てき}→〜的：09839_teki⟧: amphibious (figurative, of things or people that operate in two different domains)

WATCH OUT:
Used alone, {両生|りょうせい} sounds incomplete to native speakers; it is almost always attached to ⟦{類|るい}→類：15121_rui⟧ or ⟦{的|てき}→〜的：09839_teki⟧.
